description:
Hi! I'm a Computer Science and AI student with a strong interest in Data Analysis and Earth Science. I have experience working with Python, Pandas, data cleaning, data visualization, and statistical analysis.

I'm excited to participate in NASA Space Apps Challenge, collaborate with passionate people, and use data to explore real-world environmental challenges.

Let's build something meaningful together!
summary:
Our project focuses on understanding how Egypt’s climate has changed over the past 25 years (2001–2025) using data from NASA POWER. We collected and analyzed temperature and precipitation data, then developed an interactive Power BI dashboard to make the results easier to explore and understand.

The dashboard shows how temperature and rainfall have changed over time, compares the four seasons, and highlights differences between Eastern and Western Egypt. It also includes statistical analysis to help identify climate trends and determine whether the changes are statistically significant.

We chose this challenge because climate change is becoming increasingly important, especially in a country like Egypt where water resources, agriculture, and daily life are affected by climate conditions. Our goal is to turn raw climate data into clear, useful insights that can help people better understand these changes and support informed decisions.
details:
Our project analyzes climate changes in Egypt between 2001 and 2025 using NASA POWER data, focusing on temperature and precipitation. We used Python to clean, prepare, and analyze the data, then built an interactive Power BI dashboard to visualize climate trends, seasonal differences, and variations between Eastern and Western Egypt.

The dashboard combines maps, charts, and statistical analysis to help users understand how climate conditions have changed over time and whether these trends are statistically significant.

Our goal is to make climate data easier to understand, raise awareness of regional climate changes, and provide useful insights that can support future research and decision-making, especially in agriculture and water resource management.
